newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - December 5.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.

- In the growing controversy over alleged illegal payments by Dunnes Stores to various party officials the Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said funds totalling 180,000 Irish pounds were paid to his Fine Gael party by Ben Dunne from 1987 to 1993.

- The deputy prime minister Dick Spring is expected to report to parliament on Thursday morning on the government's attempts to get a copy of the Price Waterhouse report voluntarily from the Dunne Family following the resignation of a minister over alleged irregular payments from Dunnes Stores.

- A Belfast man wanted for extradition to Germany on charges connected with an IRA mortar attack on a British army barracks there in June was further remanded for another week at a Dublin court on Wednesday.

- Investors will enjoy another good year in 1997 with low inflation and only modest increases in international interest rates supporting further good gains according to AIB Investment Managers (AIBIM).
- Irish shoppers and drinkers will get a foretaste next week of what it will be when the euro becomes the common currency.
- The Irish Prime Minister John Bruton on Wednesday urged the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to honour the Oslo peace accord.

- Seven Irish farmers who broke the law and used illegal growth promoters will not get bovine headage and premia scheme payments, Ireland's Minister for Agriculture, Ivan Yates, confirmed on Wednesday.
- Employers and unions appeared deadlocked on a new pay deal last night as they sought to bridge a gap of more than two percent.
- Irish police commissioner Pat Byrne has spelled out an "aggressive" offensive by the force on the country's top 20 drug godfathers.
- Spain's largest insurance group, Sistema Mapfre is expanding its operations in Ireland where it focuses on the assistance end of the non-life sector.
